Let
\[
\lambda=2(n-1),\qquad m=\binom n2 .
\]
The Smith normal form of \(M_n\) is
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{diag}\Big(
\underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{n-1},
4,
\underbrace{2(n-1),\ldots,2(n-1)}_{\frac{n^2-5n+2}{2}},
\underbrace{2n(n-1),\ldots,2n(n-1)}_{n-2},
0
\Big).
}
\]

**Solution.**  
The matrix \(B_n^TB_n\) has diagonal entries \(2\), entry \(1\) when two edges of \(K_n\) meet, and entry \(0\) otherwise. Hence
\[
M_n=2(n-2)I-A_{L(K_n)},
\]
the Laplacian of the line graph \(L(K_n)\). Thus \(M_n\) has one zero invariant factor.

First compute the rational spectrum. Since
\[
B_nB_n^T=(n-2)I_n+J_n,
\]
its eigenvalues are \(2(n-1)\) on \(\mathbf 1\), and \(n-2\) with multiplicity \(n-1\). Therefore \(B_n^TB_n\) has nonzero eigenvalues
\[
2(n-1),\quad \underbrace{n-2,\ldots,n-2}_{n-1},
\]
and zero with multiplicity \(m-n\). Hence \(M_n\) has eigenvalues
\[
0,\quad \underbrace{n,\ldots,n}_{n-1},\quad
\underbrace{2(n-1),\ldots,2(n-1)}_{m-n}.
\]
So
\[
\prod_{i=1}^{m-1} d_i
=\frac{1}{m}n^{\,n-1}\bigl(2(n-1)\bigr)^{m-n}
=4n^{n-2}\bigl(2(n-1)\bigr)^{m-n-1}.
\]

It remains to determine the invariant factors. Work prime by prime.

For primes \(p\mid n\), since \(p\nmid 2(n-1)\), the \(p\)-primary part comes from the restriction to the image of \(B_n^T\). There \(M_n\) is equivalent to
\[
nI_n-J_n,
\]
the Laplacian of \(K_n\), whose Smith form is
\[
\operatorname{diag}(1,\underbrace{n,\ldots,n}_{n-2},0).
\]
Thus primes dividing \(n\) contribute exactly \(n-2\) factors of \(n\).

For odd primes \(p\mid n-1\), reduction modulo \(p\) gives rank \(n\) for \(B_n\), so \(M_n\) has \(m-n\) dimensional kernel modulo \(p\). One of these dimensions is the genuine rational kernel, leaving \(m-n-1\) nonzero invariant factors divisible by \(p\). Their total \(p\)-adic valuation is exactly that of
\[
\bigl(2(n-1)\bigr)^{m-n-1},
\]
so these factors contribute \(2(n-1)\) in exactly \(m-n-1\) places.

For \(p=2\), because \(n\) is odd, \(2(n-1)\) is divisible by \(4\). The mod \(2\) rank of \(B_n\) is \(n-1\), so \(M_n\) has \(m-n+1\) dimensional kernel mod \(2\). Again one dimension is the rational kernel, so there are \(m-n\) even nonzero invariant factors. The total \(2\)-adic valuation is
\[
v_2\!\left(4n^{n-2}\bigl(2(n-1)\bigr)^{m-n-1}\right),
\]
so the \(2\)-primary contribution is one factor \(4\), together with \(m-n-1\) factors \(2(n-1)\).

Combining the coprime \(n\)-parts with the largest \(2(n-1)\)-parts gives the divisibility-ordered invariant factors:
\[
\underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{n-1},\quad
4,\quad
\underbrace{2(n-1),\ldots,2(n-1)}_{m-2n+1},\quad
\underbrace{2n(n-1),\ldots,2n(n-1)}_{n-2},\quad
0.
\]
Since
\[
m-2n+1=\frac{n^2-5n+2}{2},
\]
this is exactly the claimed Smith normal form.
